events.factual_description: Jazz at Lincoln Center presents the fourth annual Unity Jazz Festival on January 15-16, 2027, beginning at 6:00 PM each evening throughout Frederick P. Rose Hall. The currently announced lineup includes Arturo O'Farrill and the Afro Latin Jazz Orchestra, pianist/composer Myra Melford, and percussionist Weedie Braimah with The Hands of Time; JALC states that additional acts are still to be announced. The festival is designed as an intergenerational and multicultural survey of 21st-century jazz and music associated with jazz, with general-admission festival access and a late-night Dizzy's Club option for ticket holders.

en.why_it_matters: The draw is the collision of three very different rhythmic and improvisational worlds under one festival roof: O'Farrill's large-ensemble Afro-Latin writing, Melford's exploratory piano language, and Braimah's percussion-centered work with The Hands of Time. That makes the current lineup more than a sampler of good jazz names; it sketches a genuinely broad map of how composition, groove and improvisation can relate in contemporary jazz. The remaining TBA artists could strengthen the case further, but the announced core already clears the RADAR threshold on its own.
en.trip_verdict: Actively make room for one of the two festival nights if a New York trip overlaps, and consider the second night once the remaining lineup is announced. The two-night format and recurring festival structure give enough flexibility that it should complement, not displace, a truly singular premiere, farewell or one-off elsewhere in the itinerary.

es.why_it_matters: Lo interesante es el choque de tres mundos rítmicos e improvisatorios muy distintos bajo el mismo festival: la escritura afrolatina de gran ensamble de O'Farrill, el lenguaje exploratorio de piano de Melford y el trabajo de Weedie Braimah con The Hands of Time, donde la percusión es el centro de gravedad. Así, el cartel actual es más que una colección de buenos nombres: ya dibuja un mapa bastante amplio de cómo composición, groove e improvisación pueden convivir en el jazz contemporáneo. Los artistas todavía por anunciar pueden fortalecerlo, pero el núcleo confirmado ya cruza por sí solo el umbral del RADAR.
es.trip_verdict: Sí le haría espacio activamente a una de las dos noches si coincide con un viaje a Nueva York, y volvería a mirar la segunda cuando publiquen el resto del cartel. El formato de dos noches y el carácter recurrente del festival dan suficiente flexibilidad para que complemente, en vez de desplazar, un estreno, despedida o one-off realmente singular dentro del itinerario.
